claims.value: Fibroblasts secrete all three main kinds of connective tissue fiber: collagen, elastic and reticular fibers.
claims.quote: Three main types of fibers are secreted by fibroblasts: collagen fibers, elastic fibers, and reticular fibers.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: The polysaccharides and proteins that fibroblasts release mix with extracellular fluid into a viscous ground substance, which together with the embedded fibers forms the extracellular matrix.
claims.quote: Polysaccharides and proteins secreted by fibroblasts combine with extra-cellular fluids to produce a viscous ground substance that, with embedded fibrous proteins, forms the extra-cellular matrix.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Fibroblasts secrete the ground substance, made of proteins and the polysaccharide hyaluronic acid, in which the connective tissue fibers are embedded.
claims.quote: All of these fiber types are embedded in ground substance. Secreted by fibroblasts, ground substance is made of polysaccharides, specifically hyaluronic acid, and proteins.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Fibroblasts can move, divide by mitosis and make whichever type of connective tissue is needed.
claims.quote: Fibroblasts are motile, able to carry out mitosis, and can synthesize whichever connective tissue is needed.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: In a healing wound, fibroblasts mobilize and divide rapidly, depositing collagen that forms granulation tissue to repair the damaged tissue.
claims.quote: fibroblasts mobilize and divide rapidly to repair the damaged tissue by collagen deposition, forming granulation tissue.

source.section: 5.4 Diseases, Disorders, and Injuries of the Integumentary System
source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Fibroblasts lay down the collagen of scar tissue, whose basket-weave of fibers repairs skin without restoring its normal cellular structure.
claims.quote: Fibroblasts generate scar tissue in the form of collagen, and the bulk of repair is due to the basket-weave pattern generated by collagen fibers and does not result in regeneration of the typical cellular structure of skin.

source.section: 5.4 Diseases, Disorders, and Injuries of the Integumentary System
source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: When a bone breaks, fibroblasts produce collagen fibers that connect the broken ends.
claims.quote: Fibroblasts produce collagen fibers that connect the broken bone ends, and osteoblasts start to form spongy bone.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.
